text:
marta: Heads-up — we started seeing a P99 latency spike for short sequences (<=16 tokens) after the CUDA 56200 rollout on the H100 inference pool. Router metrics show a jump around 12:35 UTC. Example: /api/generate p99 from ~320ms -> ~680ms. Not universal but concentrated on h100-pool-2. Can reproduce on canary.

chen: Yeah I noticed anomalies on the short-batch path. KV cache hitrate is stable, batching distribution unchanged. nvprof/nsys shows we're hitting a generic matmul kernel instead of the fused attention kernel for short sequences. Looks like the kernel-selector picked a different family post-driver.

aaron: Which kernel-selector commit is on that image? We had the seqlen threshold tweak merged yesterday — could be interacting with the new driver heuristics. Share traces pls.

marta: Pasting a trimmed nsys timeline snapshot (timestamps removed):
```
[nsys] inference_task: thread start
kernel_launch: fused_attn_fast_v2 -> fallback to matmul_generic (higher time)
kernel_launch: kv_cache_copy (ok)
kernel_launch: matmul_generic (50% longer than usual)
[metrics] p99 680ms, p50 24ms
```
Also see selector debug: ``selector.log`` lines show a sudden preference score tilt toward tiling=64 fallback.

dev-bot: deploy-bot: rollout/cuda-56200 finished to prod (h100-pool-2) at 12:20 UTC — author: infra-release.

max: Ran a focused microbenchmark against a h100 with CUDA 56200. Short sequences + small batchsize (1-4) cause fallback to the slower GEMM path. Root cause appears to be the driver changing warp-level perf counters that our occupancy heuristic relies on; autotuner then re-ranked kernel candidates.

chen: Short-term mitigation options: 1) runtime override to prefer the known-good fused_attn kernel for arch=h100 and seqlen<=32; 2) reduce autotuner probe frequency / increase cooldown so we don't flip ranking aggressively after driver changes; 3) route a small % of traffic to nodes on the previous driver while we validate.

marta: Can we flip an override flag and run a 5% canary? Want to validate perf + correctness (no numerical regressions). Also will need telemetry to confirm KV/hitrate and latency.

sre-oncall: I can drive the canary routing. If you give me the runtime flag name and target value I'll apply to prod-canary and monitor. If needed I can also cordon h100-pool-2 nodes.

aaron: Proposed commands (can be staged in ops-runbook):
```bash
# force preferred kernel family on pool h100-pool-2 for short seqs
rctl set inference.kernel_selector.force_family=fastfused_attn_v1 --scope=pool:h100-pool-2 --env=prod-canary
# reduce autotuner probe rate (temporary)
rctl set inference.autotuner.probe_rate=0.1 --scope=pool:h100-pool-2 --env=prod-canary
# restart runtime to pick up flags (graceful)
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/inference-runtime -n prod
```
(These are runtime flags — will only affect the selector decision logic, not model weights.)

marta: Applying the first override now in canary. Running a perf sweep. dev-bot will report health.

dev-bot: canary-agent: applied flags to pool h100-pool-2, routing set to 5% for prod-canary. Healthchecks: 200/200, latency window 5m: p99 = 340ms (previously 680ms). No errors logged.

max: Nice — verified on microbench too, p99 back down ~330ms for short-seq. KV cache behavior unchanged. Looks like a selector ranking regression not an algorithmic perf regression.

chen: Post-mortem action items I propose:
- Patch autotuner to add a driver-change detection hook (based on driver build id) that forces a re-evaluation of kernel ranks with a controlled probe schedule.
- Add a cooldown threshold so kernel rank flips require >=1000 successful probes or a 30 minute stabilization window before global switch.
- Add a telemetry event when selector flips a high-impact kernel (attach model, seqlen distro, driver id).
- If the driver change is unavoidable, update the default selector weights for that driver family.

aaron: +1. Also add a quick fallback playbook: if canary fails or regression persists revert nodes to driver 56190 image for h100-pool-2. SRE, can you estimate time+blast radius for that rollback?

sre-oncall: Rolling back drivers requires draining the pool and reimaging nodes — estimate 45-60m downtime for the pool (we can do rolling bounce to keep availability but throughput drops). I'll draft a rollback doc and preflight checks (image artifacts, driver test job).

marta: Good. I'll open a cross-team PR to: 1) add the autotuner cooldown + driver hook, 2) add selector telemetry, 3) include the runtime override knob in the ops-runbook. Tagging everyone in the PR for review.

chen: After PR lands we'll run an A/B canary (5% -> 20% -> 50%) for 2h each before promoting. If anything odd, flip override off (rctl unset ...) and revert routing.

max: Logging note — capture kernel-launch metric (kernel_family, kernel_name) in the runtime trace so we can retro-analyze selector flips in future.

marta: Thanks all. For now canary looks healthy; leaving the override in place and we'll monitor for 2h. I'll file a short incident doc with links to traces.

sre-oncall: I'll prepare the rollback playbook and post it in #incidents if needed.

aaron: One more ask — add an automated smoke that runs after any driver bump (small-seq perf + kernel-family assertion) as a presubmit gating for infra rollouts.

marta: Agreed. Putting that on the PR too.

chen: tl;dr — regression caused by selector re-ranking after driver upgrade. Mitigated with runtime override + canary. Follow-ups: autotuner hardening, telemetry, rollback playbook, infra smoke tests.

marta: Great teamwork. Ping me if you spot any drift. :thumbsup:
